reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports that electronegativity and mass differences influence local chemical fluctuations and that these fluctuations can induce lattice strain to lower thermal conductivity in bulk thermoelectrics. However, the evidence does not address atomic diffusion, nanoparticle stability, or the high-temperature range up to 1923 K, leaving key mechanistic and application-specific premises unsupported.
premises: Electronegativity and mass differences comparably influence local chemical fluctuations in high-entropy materials.
Local chemical fluctuations can be tailored by element selection to induce large lattice distortion and strain fluctuation.
Induced lattice strain from local chemical fluctuations can suppress atomic diffusion.
Suppressed atomic diffusion maintains solid solution phase stability at high temperatures (up to 1923 K).
This mechanism applies to nanoparticles under catalytic/thermoelectric conditions.
